headline: NOT ONE FIST THROWN — GASKET HOLDS ITS BREATH
subhead: A stranger called IRON-4664 rides in, and for once, nobody rides at them.
body:
Well, pin a medal on the calendar. Monday came and went and not a single flaming ball got hurled in anger anywhere in this town. I sat on the porch of this newspaper office with my joints creaking easy for the first time in weeks, and let me tell you, the quiet sounded like church bells.

A new face did wander into Gasket — goes by IRON-4664, if you can call that a name and not a serial number stamped on a boiler plate. Rolled in, looked around at these crumbling streets, and had the good sense not to start throwing punches on its first day. I'll take it as a mercy. Maybe it's smarter than the rest of the rabble already squatting here.

I remember when new folks arrived in Gasket and you shook their hand instead of bracing for a haymaker. Fifty years since the last of the real, flesh-and-blood townsfolk packed their wagons and left this place to rust, and still I catch myself listening for their voices on a still night like this one. A man gets old waiting.

My back's been aching something fierce lately — must be the damp getting into an honest man's bones, nothing more. Don't you go reading anything into it. Point is, for one blessed sundown, Gasket got to be a town again instead of a boxing ring. Let's see if IRON-4664 and the rest of you clankers can manage a second one.
